blocks.text: The assurance of “Peace, peace” in verse 14 is exposed as false because no peace exists. Some interpreters connect later “peace and security” language with this prophetic critique of false assurance; others see Roman civic claims, ordinary complacency, or overlapping resonances. The connection remains disputed.

Jeremiah 6 belongs to a larger received book that combines poetry, prose sermons, narratives, letters, headings, repeated accounts, restoration collections, oracles concerning nations, and an appendix. A practical outline places chapters 2–25 within an early major section of the book, while the book’s long compositional and textual history remains a matter of discussion.
